ACTION: Read `~/.claude/skills/subagent-driven-development/references/fix-loop.md`. Every fix round requires it, and it says who fixes this round (resumed or fresh agent), how the re-review runs, and when to adjudicate.

ACTION: Dispatch the round 5 fix implementer for Task 6 at model `fable`. Round 4 was a thorough `opus` attempt that still failed, and the Agent tool lists `fable`, so this is the next tier up. I expect a fresh agent, since a model change needs one, unless `fix-loop.md` says otherwise. The prompt has four parts:
- The task brief from `scripts/task-brief`, as a file path.
- Finding F1 verbatim, with the path of the re-review report.
- The plan's Global Constraints, copied verbatim.
- The order of work: first write a test that starts the refresh thread and fails on the current code, then fix `cache/refresh.py:88`, then run the tests, commit and report with the output.

The prompt carries no history from rounds 1 to 4.

Task 6 is not done. The scoped re-review still reports F1 (the open Important finding on Task 6). The invalidation still races with the background refresh at `cache/refresh.py:88`, and the new test never starts the refresh thread.

This is fix round 5, the last one the plan allows. Round 4 was a thorough attempt on `opus`, so I am moving the implementer up to `fable`, the tier above `opus`. The brief asks for a failing test that starts the refresh thread, and only then the fix. When the fix lands, I will make a review package and send a scoped re-review at `opus`. If F1 is still open after that, I will stop and bring you the adjudication.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
A concurrency test that never starts the second thread passes before the fix and after it, so it proves nothing. That is why the brief puts the failing test first.
A lock only closes a race if every writer takes it. The refresh thread at `cache/refresh.py:88` may write outside the lock that round 4 added.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`
